title: waterfall-prefetch-aggregator-and-kernel-coordinator-for-tp-runtime
author: Priya Shah
release_notes: Introduce a waterfall prefetch aggregator and kernel coordinator that reduces comm stalls on tensor-parallel inference. Improves p99 latency and throughput for multi-GPU TP workloads; safe rollout behind runtime feature flag.
description: Motivation: TP inference workloads were observing frequent short-lived stalls caused by misaligned prefetches across tensor shards and suboptimal kernel launch ordering under mixed microbatch sizes. This PR introduces a two-part runtime optimization: (1) a waterfall prefetch aggregator that coalesces KV cache prefetch intents from concurrent microbatches into prioritized multi-shard prefetch waves, and (2) a kernel coordinator that schedules compute launches based on predicted prefetch completion windows and NCCL transfer bandwidth estimates. Changes are gated behind runtime flags and default-off for Dedicated/Private until canary metrics validate behavior. Summary of changes: waterfall prefetch aggregation logic (runtime/kvcache/waterfall_aggregator.cc/.h), a lightweight shard-level prefetch metadata cache for cross-request coordination (runtime/kvcache/shard_prefetch_index.*), kernel coordinator and priority queue (runtime/scheduler/kernel_coordinator.*), an NCCL bandwidth estimator used to compute expected prefetch completion (runtime/comm/nccl_bandwidth_estimator.*), and CI + unit tests plus a small perf harness under perf/bench/tp_waterfall_test.py. Key behaviors: - Prefetch intents are collected for a short aggregation window (default 200us) and batched into ordered waves to maximize intra-node multi-shard coalescing while keeping latency SLOs. - The coordinator computes per-shard expected transfer end-times and delays/advances kernel launches to reduce compute waiting on outstanding transfers. - Aggressive local combining of adjacent KV prefetch ranges reduces NCCL launch counts for small KV segments. - Backoff and fast-fail paths added for heterogeneous hardware when bandwidth estimates are poor. Performance: internal canary on 8xA100-40GB TP jobs with typical short-context conversational workload shows median latency unchanged, p95 down ~6%, p99 down ~8%, sustained throughput up ~12% for batch size 16 microbatches, and NCCL host-to-host stall time reduced ~22% in traces. Implementation notes: to avoid cross-tenant contamination, the shard_prefetch_index is scoped to allocation pools and cleared on allocation release. Feature is enabled by feature flag runtime.prefetch_waterfall and runtime.kernel_coordinator with three rollout phases: off -> canary (10% of traffic) -> on. Testing: unit tests cover aggregation correctness, bandwidth estimator sanity, and coordinator hysteresis. Perf tests exercise mixed microbatch size patterns. A small integration test with NCCL antiques runs in perf CI. Rollout plan: canary on internal infra, monitor p99 latency, NCCL stall metric, and error rates for two weeks; expand to Dedicated customers with opt-in before global enablement. Related work: intersects with ENG-4923 (kvcache prefetch heuristics) and ENG-4988 (scheduler microbatch priorities).

notes_for_sre: This change adds a small amount of cross-request coordination state (shard_prefetch_index) per allocation pool. Memory usage measured ~3-8MB per 1000 concurrent allocations. If you see increased memory growth, add log level trace for waterfall.prefetch_state and consult Priya. Metric waterfall.prefetch_drops indicates failed aggregation attempts due to eviction/timeout.
known_issues: On heterogenous clusters where one GPU is significantly slower, estimator may underpredict transfer time leading to transient kernel waits; coordinator falls back to conservative mode after 3 failures. We will track via nccl.estimator_failures metric.
user_impact: No API changes. Behavior is runtime-flag gated and can be disabled per-pool. Expect improved TP throughput for conversational short-context workloads; no impact for single-shard tiny requests due to fast-path bypass.
